title: Are there merits to "Worst Of" Lists?

commenti.body:
The way I see it - there’s art that’s good and there’s art that’s interesting. The ten worst movies of the year will probably be more interesting than the good-but-forgettable movies that would be in the middle between best and worst. 

Also film is a unique medium for this subject - where unlike books or music - watching a bad movie isn’t tedious or unpleasant and can be very stimulating instead.

Stuff like that Variety article is kind of going after two things: one negativity can sometimes drive more engagement than positivity. A lot of big publications post very same-y best of lists so the worst of list stands out. Two, it’s very clearly meant to drive hate clicks. Including Asteroid City is a pure troll job, if the writer didn’t like it that’s whatever, but comparing it to total non films like Ghosted or The Flash is insulting. 

Personally I don’t see the value in making or talking about a worst of list. I watch films with the intent of liking them and usually there’s not much to talk about if I think a film is bad. Like yes The Flash is hideous looking garbage but I’d much rather talk about the good films I saw this year.

I don't do a full "top ten" each year, but I do list the notable ones annually. My notable list of worst movies this year was:

Cocaine Bear

El Conde

Hypnotic

The Expendables 4

Five Nights at Freddy's

None of those are small guys just trying to make a movie. These are movies with real money behind them, so I feel OK calling them out for their poor quality.

The only kind of "worst of" lists that I respect and appreciate are ones where the author actually puts in the work to find truly awful films. Because the *actual* worst movies of the year are not going have been seen by many people, will often be very low budget, and will often take some work to track down.

If your "worst of" list is just a hyperbolic title for a "popular films I think are overrated" list, then I have no patience for it. People who write lists like that ought to just write a long form critique of the film they thought was overrrated.

I mean not that I don’t disagree with everything you are saying. And I actually don’t brag he with worst of list for the reason you said. 

If you really don’t like a movie in this case asteroid city and you did find it just as bad as the flash then like why not mention it. Now I don’t know the writers motives and yeah it might just be about increasing engagement. 

But literally all movie opinions are subjective. I’ve absolutely loved some critically hated movie and I’ve soo disliked critically adored movies as much as movie I think is universally agreed as bad. 

I might be trying to play devils advocate since I similarly disliked asteroid city and it’s on the bottom of my 2023 list. 

This discourse reminds a bit of what a reviewer I follow said about the semi backlash the letterbox four best movies that Emma stone did. For those who are not aware the cast of poor things largely picked unconventional movies and were accused of being pretensions amongst other things which I would argue is silly. Anyway the reviewer was sorta arguing that a lot of people when they are confronted with someone else not liking a movie they like they treat it as a personal attack. That the mere idea of not liking a movie is somehow invalidating your own experience. 

All to say it’s hard to tell with articles that rely on engagement. But the existence of someone not liking a movie like asteroid city is not inherently bait

Back in the day these lists could be fun and had some credibility because you had a group of people who had seen most of the movies and their opinion was valid.  Present day, all lists are either trolling or they are so desperate to try to get trending that they make an opinion that is so blatantly bad that the whole list can be viewed as a joke.  Again they used to be fun now they are just another thing to roll your eyes at.

I think an interesting list that’s better than “Worst Of” would be “What could have been”. I think that’s something that would lead to a more fun discussion. For instance, I didn’t think the new Indian Jones movie was awful, but I thought that it had so much untapped potential. I got more out of talking about the different creative changes I would have made in order to get the most out of it.

I actually want to watch a truly terrible film , not just an overrated one. 
If you're the bottom of one list ,you're the top of another. So take heart filmakers.

Maybe this is going to come across as snobbish, idk, but if someone sincerely thinks that Asteroid City is as bad as The Flash then they are not a serious person, should not be taken seriously, and ideally should not be having their film “criticism” posted in a pretty major publication. 

Obviously film criticism is subjective but IMO a lot of the criticism of Asteroid City is shallow and in the case of that Variety article very clearly coming from someone who just patently refused to engage with the film. I’m biased I guess because it’s one of my favorites of the year and a top 2-3 Anderson film of all time for me, but I’m willing to engage with good faith and well thought out criticism of it or any film. The Variety article isn’t that though.

I think if you're rating the worst movies of all time - - perhaps.

But if it's of the year I don't really think particularly meritable.

A list presumes that one has watched pretty much all available theatrical release films-- and maybe some critics and avid movie watchers do, but I don't think most of the general public does and I'm not the best at keeping up with movies.

The thing though is that movies of different genres that aren't particularly good have different flaws, which I feel makes criticism more difficult to do fairly - - because then you hypothetically can get lazy with criticism, and so then something could be stated like this rom-com isn't paced like a James Bond action thriller.. I'm barely kidding with this one.

I also feel like it can date publications - - kind of like when the Razzies nominated Shelly Duvall for her performance in The Shining. 

Finally my  biggest complaint is.. Do you want Babylon ( or its 2023 equivalent) to ascend into the heavens of counterreview hype?

Yeah I have n read the worst list since I actively try not to engage with that sorta discourse. I guess I’m just open minded. Someone telling them they just didn’t like x movie or found it boring would be enough for me. 

Maybe I’m biased in toner way since I love Wes Anderson and I didn’t care for asteroid city either so I’m more open to people not liking it. Or other movies frankly.

I think this is key, these lists have value if they're *fun*. They can contain films that are so bad it's good, and thus provide second hand entertainment, or they can be the result of someone trudging through truly horrible movies and hopefully also be a clever writer.
Hate doesn't get more clicks. It's just easier to push out that type of content.

Sure. I saw every movie you mentioned and thought each one was a fucking piece on shit on a shingle. It’s the worst year for film I’ve ever experienced. Everything is a huge fucking turd. Please publish Worst Of lists so this rotten stinking year filled with turds never happens again. I’m offended by how bad everything is. South Park inventing the Panderverse is perfect timing.

I think the issue for me is that a “Worst Of” list, taken literally, is a bottomless pit. The true “worst movie of 2023”, let alone the “worst movie of all time”, is probably something no one but the filmmaker has even seen. And it’s just silly to me to say something like “Ant-Man: Quantumania is the worst movie of 2023”. You would need to at least qualify that with “…that got a wide release” or “…with a budget over $X million”.

That being said, there is merit to highlighting bad movies in a “what went wrong here?” sense, but a Top 10 list is a bad vehicle for that, in my opinion.
You say that, but then Alien Beasts exist, and I really doubt that you'll want to sit through it.

I think there's a place for "worst use of money and talent"-lists. Telling people who sell themselves short to do better. The Razzies, that give awards for worst sequel or prequel for instance, that's nice because it is a push for filmmakers to do better.

Negative reviews have their place. They uphold standards for the medium, and when well written, can be deliciously fun.

I actually think certain media need more negativity in reviews, especially literature. Major publications almost never publish negative book reviews anymore, and I find that professional book reviews have become a poor indicator of quality. The Economist published some [evidence](https://www.economist.com/culture/2023/07/21/critics-are-getting-less-cruel-alas) to that effect (apologies for paywall).

IMO film reviews are the best “calibrated” of any media right now — sure there are cases where the consensus misses the point of a film, and awards notoriously age poorly, but I’d argue that’s actually improved in the last 20 years or so.

I’m not sure if there is value in the lists but I think there is absolutely value in watching bad movies. First off there is the “so bad it is good factor” which really means hanging out with friends and having fun riffing on it. It’s more the social element. 

Beyond that there is the value of seeing bad things so you can appreciate the good even more. You’ll appreciate the height of the mountain more after climbing out of the valley…or that line of thought.

Most importantly there is an intention element. I once had a friend who rated all bad movies high. I wondered why for long time. But I think it was the intrigue of it all. What was the intention behind the execution. Even if they didn’t reach it, what were they going for. Where in the path to greatness did it fall apart. Understanding why a movie fails can be just as important to understanding why a movie succeeds.

I think there's a difference between negative reviews and "worst of" lists. The former, as you said, are necessary and I find that even the harshest of (professional written, mind you) the criticisms don't come with a sneering smile.

I find that a lot of "worst of" lists aren't criticism in that sense, though. They seem more driven by schadenfreude than anything else -- a sort of, "look how bad these movies were, can you believe they were greenlit" kind of tone.

That's not negative criticism; that's just snobbery, and I'm not drawn to that sort of perspective.

I 100% agree with watching bad movies (an old film professor of mine once said that watching bad films is often more educational and interesting than watching masterpieces). And I think most "bad" films aren't so horrendous they deserve to be shuffled out of the bar, so to speak. Rather, they often the result of either missed opportunities or little mistakes that add up (i.e. characterizations that feel shallow, pacing that jerks around a bit too much, etc.)   


Of the \~3,000 films I've seen, maybe 50 qualify as true stinkers that I couldn't find much value in. Everything else had at least one element that was interesting, captivating, or well crafted.

I see your point. But maybe the issue isn’t lists per se, it’s just that the “listicle” format is associated with lazy, SEO optimized writing?

I guess I don’t see why *in principle* a negative review in list format would be bad, ie an explanation of the films that fell shortest of their potential in a given year… it doesn’t seem any worse than a list of the best films.

But I definitely agree that articles in that format would tend toward lower quality in practice.

>There's a self-serving nature to "Worst Of" lists, and a smarminess, that I don't gravitate toward. 

I suppose my controversial response would be that most year-end roundup articles pretending they aren't brainlessly regurgitating what everyone else has already said about the most talked about movies of that year are also smarmy and self-serving. You can make really commentary out of anything, but it's a needle in a haystack regardless of the subject matter.
It definitely can in certain situations, the inclusion of asteroid city on that list is the sole reason is spread like crazy on Twitter

It's sensationalism at this point. One guy had AC as his second worst movie of the year, yet Variety's headline was "The Worst Movies of 2023". It's impressions-baiting, and I say that as someone who thought Asteroid City was a mess and that Wes Anderson has gotten lazy.

It's just a weird time for those kinda lists. I used to enjoy them as pure "oh yeah the fuck Emoji Movie, that sucked" kinda content. Things you read though during a lunch break. Everything in wide release at this point though are either calculated franchise/IP movies that will get enough points for at least following story structure and having decent name-actors in them, or the curated Oscar players. Some stinkers still fall through, but at this point those lists are just schlocky netflix movies, theatrical flops, bad horror movies, and then a divisive movie like Beau is Afraid.

Basically, it should either be someone who has watched a lot of that years movies and is truly delivering the worst 5 or whatever, or someone who has legitimate gripes with a set of middling/divisive/mainstream/popular/etc. movies. Like, if I had a list, I'd probably have Elvis on it last year. I enjoyed Austin Butler in it, but I thought that movie was a disaster.

Basically, you can do it if you have an honest take.

It depends completely on whether or not the people publishing the list are profiting off of engagement, the Asteroid City example — listed alongside The Flash — is purposefully provocative because the ad revenue it brings in from scandalized readers fuels the entire online newsletter industry. Now, some random person on letterboxd who I personally find to consistently write quality reviews? Of course I'm going to read about why they think Barbie blows, there's nothing for them to gain but likes and comments.

I would recommend Cranium Intel (2016).

It’s so bad that it genuinely pushes the limits of what qualifies as a film.
Neil Breen released a new film this year...

I enjoy a genuinely terrible movie, and I'm not sure how to square that with finding worst of lists distasteful.. Like Lauren Lapkus was nominated for "worst actress" for the wrong missy. I think this is a fundementally an insult to the funiest actor in a shitty movie. Why should Lauren Lapkus get an insult award for being the saving grace of a movie?

So much of it is engagement bait but I do think there is some merit to analyzing things like The Flash which is not only a bad movie but representative of an element of the rot in the industry chasing derivative sequels with huge budgets. Or like those netflix streamers like Heart of Stone or The Grey Man. But you can do that in a much better way than just saying they're the worst of the year. 

And on the other hand there are always going to be popular movies that you hate or vice versa and there can be interesting discussion there (well, not much with the structures of social media and film stan culture) 

But yeah I'm always much more interested in reading why someone loved a movie than why they hated it, although sometimes a great takedown is a treat, especially if it's a consensus favorite that you also hate!

I agree with you about the real worst films not making these sorts of lists, but any real 'worst of' list would basically just be bullying. I'm not a huge fan of the lists as they are, but I'd find them orders of magnitude more unbearable if all they did was mock people trying and failing to express themselves on 4-figure budgets.

I used to work a small-time distribution company, the kind of company you'd go to when every other indie distributor rejected your film. People have *no idea* how bad a movie can be. If you watched *every* movie made in a given year, nothing released in theaters would be below a 7 out of 10.

Was Hypnotic really that bad? I haven't seen it (and don't expect much more than b-movie flair) but by the look of it it seems to be an improvement over Robert Rodriguez late green screen adventures. Or so I hoped.
I thought Hypnotic was embarrassing. Not one interesting moment or twist in the entire thing. Looked bad, too.
Exactly. It's what's so frustrating about all those 1/10 and 10/10 scores people leave on review websites. Hyperbolic and unhelpful.

It's not "bullying" to express an opinion about a product being sold to the public in exchange for $. I'm not talking about tracking down someone's first student film project and mocking it for the world to see. This is about films that get some kind of distribution, probably straight to DVD or streaming.

Once you put yourself out there and ask for money in exchange for your creation, you open yourself up to criticism.

I get a kick out of them because they can be quite amusing. I re-watched Siskel and Ebert's Worst of specials frequently. However, I consider all rankings of films to be limited. There's a vast spectrum of films released every year and you can't cover everything. Also, we all have different tastes. I have Ioved films that have been trashed by critics and the contrary. I think true film fans need to abandon of a canon of artistic triumphs and dismal failures. Or, simply stress that any rankings of films on any lists is an entirely subjective.

There aren't any merits to worst of lists.

We live in a time where film discussion already leads to toxic discourse, and having a "worst of" list is the same as the toxic discourse that many critics claim to be above, but are actually helping to drive by making a "worst of" list.

Are these usually sent direct to video? I don't have any theaters near me that aren't part of a big chain, and I love small indie films. Even bad ones since they help me appreciate good ones more.

Where can I find these films?

I worked there a long time ago, when dvds were still popular.

I assume it's all dumped on streaming now, but not the kind of places where the algorithm will recommend them to anyone.
